WF-2025-014.aiChallenges: Landlord retaliation was significantly more frequent than anticipated — 16 tribunal defences were required against a budget of 8, exhausting the legal costs line by month nine and requiring reserves to cover the shortfall. A structural gap also emerged: even a successful HHSRS improvement notice does not guarantee repairs, as four landlords simply sold the property with the tenant still in situ, leaving those households' situations unresolved.
WF-2025-014.aiLessons: Tenants typically approach the service only after approximately a year of living with damp, by which point conditions are severe and cases more complex. The charity found that health visitors — not council referral routes — are the most effective pathway to reach households early, and has redirected its outreach accordingly.

WF-2025-023.aiChallenges: Mentor supervision proved under-resourced in the original budget — fortnightly paid supervision was the minimum viable level, not a comfortable one, and funds had to be moved from the training line to sustain it. One mentor withdrew mid-placement following a bereavement, requiring a young person to be re-matched and effectively restarting that relationship from scratch.
WF-2025-023.aiLessons: Nine months with a defined ending works significantly better than an open-ended relationship: all four open-ended trial matches drifted without resolution, demonstrating that the structured exit plan is what makes the relationship purposeful rather than an administrative formality. programmeAlignment.narrative: This project is a near-perfect fit for the Warm Homes programme goal: it provides casework that resolves the underlying problem (income maximisation, retrofit referral, tariff switching) rather than a one-off payment, it targets hard-to-heat concessionary-coal-era housing with no central heating, and the van-based outreach model is precisely designed to reach households that would not otherwise come forward. There is no fuel-voucher element and the referral pathway into the council retrofit scheme addresses the structural problem of cold homes.

WF-2025-041.aiChallenges: An unplanned gearbox failure in month seven took the van off the road for three weeks; a reduced service run from village halls was put in place but attendance dropped sharply, revealing that the van itself (not just the presence of advisers) is a key driver of footfall. The team budgeted a vehicle contingency reserve for the following year to mitigate recurrence.
WF-2025-041.aiLessons: Fixed, unchanging weekly visit times proved far more important than anticipated: in the two villages where the day was varied to accommodate other commitments, attendance was roughly half that of villages with a consistent slot, suggesting that reliability of timing is as important as the service itself. The van breakdown further confirmed that the physical format of the service — not just its location — is central to why people engage.
